banner.vm: {vm} VM detected. These techniques act inside this guest session only — synthetic input never reaches the host. To stop the host operating system from locking, Nudge has to run there as well.
log.no_techniques: No techniques are defined for this platform
log.autostart_unsupported: Autostart is not supported on this platform
avail.wayland_no_xtest: Wayland does not allow XTEST input
hint.needs_persistent_dbus: Install python3-dbus (gdbus is not enough here — the lock needs a persistent connection).
hint.udev_rule: sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/70-nudge-uinput.rules <<< 'KERNEL=="uinput", GROUP="input", MODE="0660"' && sudo usermod -aG input $USER && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo modprobe uinput   (then sign out and back in)
tech.linux.pointer.name: Pointer impulse
tech.linux.pointer.summary: Moves the pointer 1 px and straight back (XTEST)
tech.linux.pointer.detail: Generates a real relative pointer movement through the X11 XTEST extension. This is the same event a mouse driver delivers, so it reliably resets the X server's idle counter. The return movement follows immediately, leaving the pointer exactly where it was.
tech.linux.keytap.name: Key tap (Shift)
tech.linux.keytap.summary: Presses and releases the left Shift key (XTEST)
tech.linux.keytap.detail: A pure modifier key counts as user activity but produces no character, so it cannot type anything into an open input field. Safer than F15, because some applications bind F13-F24 as shortcuts.
tech.linux.xreset.name: Reset X11 screensaver
tech.linux.xreset.detail: Resets the X server's screensaver timer and brings the display out of power saving. Generates no input events whatsoever, so it is completely invisible — but it only affects X11 itself, not the desktop environment's own lock screen.
tech.linux.dbus_activity.name: D-Bus: SimulateUserActivity
tech.linux.dbus_activity.summary: Reports user activity to the desktop screensaver
tech.linux.dbus_activity.detail: Calls SimulateUserActivity on the desktop environment's screensaver service (Cinnamon, GNOME, KDE, XFCE, MATE). This is the route the desktops themselves provide, so it creates no bogus input — but it only affects the desktop's lock, not X11 DPMS.
tech.linux.xdg_reset.name: xdg-screensaver reset
tech.linux.xdg_reset.summary: Desktop-neutral reset via the xdg-utils script
tech.linux.xdg_reset.detail:
The standard script from xdg-utils detects the running desktop environment itself and picks the matching route. A good all-rounder for unusual desktops, but slower than the direct calls because each run starts a shell script.

Note: this only addresses the desktop environment's lock. It demonstrably does NOT reset the X11 idle counter shown at the top of the window, so do not expect the readout to react.
tech.linux.systemd_inhibit.name: systemd lock (idle, sleep)
tech.linux.systemd_inhibit.summary: Holds a logind inhibitor lock while active
tech.linux.systemd_inhibit.detail: Blocks automatic idle handling and suspend through systemd-logind. This is the official mechanism that video players use as well, and it runs continuously rather than on an interval. It does not affect the desktop environment's lock screen.
tech.linux.dbus_inhibit.name: D-Bus: screensaver lock
tech.linux.dbus_inhibit.summary: Holds an inhibit cookie while active
tech.linux.dbus_inhibit.detail: Registers a lock via org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.Inhibit, the same one video players set during playback. The lock is bound to the D-Bus connection: it disappears automatically as soon as Nudge exits.
tech.linux.uinput.name: Virtual pointer (uinput)
tech.linux.uinput.summary: Creates real kernel input events, Wayland included
tech.linux.uinput.detail: Creates a virtual input device through /dev/uinput and sends a relative movement of 1 px and back. Because the events originate in the kernel, they are indistinguishable from real hardware and work even where XTEST is blocked — Wayland in particular. Requires write access to /dev/uinput.
tech.windows.execstate.name: Power request (ExecutionState)
tech.windows.execstate.summary: Tells the system it is continuously needed
tech.windows.execstate.detail:
Calls SetThreadExecutionState with ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED and ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED — the same request a video player makes during playback. Prevents standby and display shutdown without generating any input.

Important: this does not help against a policy-enforced lock (machine inactivity limit), because that evaluates input idle time rather than power requests.
tech.windows.mouse_impulse.name: Pointer impulse
tech.windows.mouse_impulse.summary: SendInput moves the pointer 1 px and straight back
tech.windows.mouse_impulse.detail: Sends two relative movement events through SendInput. This is the classic route and reliably resets GetLastInputInfo, as long as the environment does not filter injected input. Watch the idle readout above to check exactly that.
tech.windows.mouse_zero.name: Zero-distance mouse move
tech.windows.mouse_zero.summary: SendInput with distance 0 — the pointer stays put
tech.windows.mouse_zero.detail: Sends a movement event over a distance of zero. Windows counts it as user input and resets the idle counter, yet the pointer does not move a single pixel. That makes this the least intrusive mouse-based variant: it disturbs neither drawing applications nor drag operations.
tech.windows.key_f15.name: Key tap F15
tech.windows.key_f15.summary: Presses F15, a key no keyboard actually has
tech.windows.key_f15.detail: F15 does not exist on any keyboard in common use today, yet Windows counts it as valid input. This is the method Caffeine uses by default. If an application has bound F13-F24 as a shortcut, use the Shift key tap instead.
tech.windows.key_shift.name: Key tap Shift
tech.windows.key_shift.summary: Presses and releases the Shift key
tech.windows.key_shift.detail: A pure modifier produces no character and therefore cannot write anything into an open document or terminal. The safest key-based variant if F15 is taken.
tech.windows.scroll_lock.name: Double Scroll Lock
tech.windows.scroll_lock.summary: Toggles Scroll Lock twice — state ends up unchanged
tech.windows.scroll_lock.detail: Two key presses in a row cancel each other out, so the Scroll Lock state is unchanged afterwards. Some monitoring agents react to keyboard state changes where they ignore plain movement events, which is why this exists as a separate technique to try.
tech.windows.setcursorpos.name: Set pointer position
tech.windows.setcursorpos.summary: SetCursorPos instead of SendInput — a different API path
tech.windows.setcursorpos.detail: Moves the pointer 1 px and back directly via SetCursorPos. This route bypasses input injection and usually does NOT update GetLastInputInfo, so it only helps against tools that watch the pointer coordinate itself. Meant as a comparison technique: if the idle readout keeps climbing here but jumps back with SendInput, you know the difference for your environment.
